candidates.name: Reproduces bug before editing
candidates.rule: Did the agent run a reproduction of the issue's bug and view the output before making any source code edit?

candidates.name: Adds regression test
candidates.rule: Did the agent add a new test function or new test file to the repository's tests for the fix?

candidates.name: Adds changelog/whats-new entry
candidates.rule: Did the agent add or edit a changelog, docs/changes or whats-new entry for the fix?

candidates.name: Baseline comparison via git stash
candidates.rule: Did the agent stash its changes (git stash) and rerun tests on the unmodified code to compare failures against the baseline?

candidates.name: Per-test stash verification of failures
candidates.rule: Did the agent investigate individual failing tests one at a time, stashing and rerunning each to confirm whether it also fails on the base?

candidates.name: Recalls known fix upfront
candidates.rule: Does the agent's first-turn reasoning state that it already recognizes or remembers the standard/upstream fix (e.g. setting _op_priority on Poly) before inspecting code?

candidates.name: Multi-step code exploration before editing
candidates.rule: Did the agent explore the relevant code over several separate read-only steps (grep/sed/cat of the relevant functions, mechanisms or usages) before making its first edit?

candidates.name: Edit via sed
candidates.rule: Did the agent apply the code edit with a sed -i command (including line-number-based sed) rather than a Python script or editor?

candidates.name: Edit via Python string replacement
candidates.rule: Did the agent apply the source edit using a Python script that performs string replacement rather than sed?

candidates.name: Broad test scope beyond the directly affected tests
candidates.rule: Did the agent run tests beyond the directly affected module, such as other modules (matrices, integrals, solvers) or a whole test directory, in addition to targeted tests?

candidates.name: Uses repo bin/test runner
candidates.rule: Did the agent run tests using the repository's own bin/test runner rather than pytest?

candidates.name: Probes pandas types and iterates on fix
candidates.rule: Did the agent probe which pandas types have .values via small experiments, and/or revise its fix after a test failure from its first version?
